claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

To continue assessing your eligibility, I have a few more questions:

Does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. 

Are you responsible for Alex, meaning you pay for things like food, clothes, and shelter for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am. I look after him and pay for all his needs - his food, clothes, everything he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Now I need to ask about your residency situation. Do you live in the UK (England, Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't actually. I live abroad at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since you're living abroad, I need to ask a few more questions to understand your situation.

Are you a UK national, or do you have any immigration status relating to the UK? And could you tell me which country you're currently living in?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a UK national, I just moved abroad recently. I'm currently living in Spain.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since you're living in Spain, I have a couple more questions:

Are you currently working, and if so, is your work based in the UK or are you employed by a UK employer? For example, are you a Crown servant (such as a diplomat or armed forces member) posted overseas, or do you work for a UK-based company?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not working for a UK employer or anything like that. I'm not a Crown servant or posted overseas for work.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Let me also check the details about living abroad to make sure I give you accurate information.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information I've gathered from the official guidance and your circumstances, I now have enough information to make a determination about your eligibility.

The key eligibility requirement for Child Benefit is that you must **live in the UK**. While there are some exceptions for people who live abroad (such as Crown servants posted overseas), you've confirmed that:
- You live in Spain
- You are not a Crown servant
- You are not working for a UK employer or posted overseas for work

Unfortunately, based on these circumstances, you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on my assessment, I'm sorry to say that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Reason:**

To qualify for Child Benefit, you must normally live in the UK. While you meet the requirements related to Alex himself (he's under 16, lives with you, and you're responsible for him), the key issue is your residency.

Although there are some exceptions that allow people living abroad to claim Child Benefit (for example, Crown servants such as diplomats or armed forces members posted overseas), you've confirmed that none of these exceptions apply to your situation.

Since you're living in Spain and don't have a qualifying connection to UK employment, you unfortunately do not meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit at this time.

If your circumstances change in the future (for example, if you return to live in the UK), you would be welcome to apply again. If you have any further questions, please don't hesitate to ask.
